Threat.value: Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience
Having strong negative feelings such as fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame

Negative Appraisals.value: I feel guilty for surviving when others did not

issues.item: Physical Vulnerability: My body has been permanently damaged by what happened
issues.explanation: For trauma to a loved one, the appraisal that the patient's own body has been permanently damaged is hard to reconcile unless the patient was also directly physically injured; that direct-injury theme is not supported elsewhere in the profile.

issues.item: Back to Wall: I feel unsafe unless my back is against a wall where I can see the room
issues.explanation: Threat items center on personal physical danger and hypervigilance in the environment ('back to wall', exaggerated startle), which fits direct personal assault/combat trauma more than trauma to a loved one, and is not well linked to the reported appraisal content.

issues.item: Sleep Vigilance: I have difficulty falling asleep because I need to stay alert
issues.explanation: For trauma to a loved one, this item implies an ongoing need to guard against immediate external danger to oneself. That does not fit well with the rest of the profile, which centers on bereavement-related cognitions (survival guilt, numbness) rather than personal threat exposure. It is also weakly aligned with the formulation, where Threat is linked mainly with Negative Appraisals and not with trigger-driven hyperarousal or ongoing danger monitoring.

The threat items are dominated by nonspecific hyperarousal and reminder reactivity, which usually implies trigger-linked activation, but the formulation specifies Triggers → Threat as inactive. With no trigger content present, 'physical reactions when reminded' is poorly aligned with the stated formulation structure.

'Mistrust: People can't be trusted' is a broad interpersonal appraisal that is not well anchored to trauma to a loved one in the rest of this profile. The other appraisal items center on guilt and emotional deadness, but pervasive mistrust suggests a different trauma pattern and lacks support from the selected threat items.

vignette: Kiet's eyes would lock onto the horizon, scanning for any sign of trouble as he navigated his fishing boat through the choppy waters of the Gulf. It had been three years since his son, Linh, was lost at sea during a routine fishing trip. Kiet was certain that if only he had been more vigilant, more cautious, Linh would still be alive today. This guilt gnawed at him, making him feel dead inside – as though all joy and warmth had been extinguished. As the days turned into weeks, and the weeks into months, Kiet began to notice changes in himself. He was always on edge, his senses heightened, waiting for the other shoe to drop. The sound of seagulls would send a shiver down his spine, reminding him of that fateful day when Linh didn't return. His sleep became fitful and erratic – he'd lie awake at night, replaying every moment leading up to Linh's disappearance, wondering what he could've done differently. Kiet's mistrust of others grew as well; he couldn't shake the feeling that people were hiding something from him. He'd become withdrawn, pushing away his friends and family – even his wife, Tuyet. She tried to be supportive, but Kiet just felt like she didn't understand what he was going through. As the months passed, these physical reactions intensified – his heart racing whenever he saw a boat in distress or heard the sound of waves crashing against the shore. He'd become convinced that every wave held some hidden danger, waiting to snatch away someone else he loved. This fear fueled his hypervigilance, making him even more prone to jump at every little thing. His emotional numbness made it hard for Kiet to connect with others – or even himself. He'd go through the motions of daily life without any sense of purpose or meaning. His relationships began to fray; Tuyet would try to talk to him about Linh, but he just couldn't bear it. It was as if speaking his son's name out loud would unleash a torrent of emotions he wasn't prepared to face. One day, while Kiet was out fishing, a sudden storm rolled in – the same kind that had claimed Linh's life. As the winds howled and lightning flashed across the sky, Kiet felt himself transported back to that terrible night. His body went into overdrive – his heart racing, his senses on high alert. In that moment, all his worst fears came flooding back: the thought of losing Tuyet or someone else he cared about; the feeling of being powerless against nature's fury. Kiet returned home that evening, shaken to his core. He knew then that he couldn't keep going on like this – something had to give. It was time for him to face his demons head-on and work through the guilt, mistrust, and emotional numbness that had taken hold of his life. With a newfound sense of determination, Kiet decided it was time to seek help – before his memories consumed him completely.
